name: Adult Census Income Database
description: The Adult dataset, also known as the Census Income dataset, was extracted by Ronny Kohavi and Barry Becker from the 1994 United States Census Bureau database. The task is to predict whether an individual's annual income exceeds $50,000 based on 14 demographic and employment attributes such as age, education, marital status, occupation, and race.

name: California Housing Prices Database
description: The California Housing dataset contains metrics derived from the 1990 U.S. Census for 20,640 census block groups in California. Originally developed by R. Kelley Pace and Ronald Barry, the regression target is the median house value for California districts, predicted using features such as median income, housing median age, total rooms, total bedrooms, population, households, latitude, and longitude.

While underlying 1990 US Census data is generally not subject to US copyright, the compiled regression dataset lacks a formal authoritative public domain or open source license declaration.

description: The CIFAR-10 dataset consists of 60,000 32x32 colour images across 10 mutually exclusive classes, with 6,000 images per class. Subdivided into 50,000 training images and 10,000 test images, collected by Alex Krizhevsky, Vinod Nair, and Geoffrey Hinton.

name: Mozilla Common Voice
description: Mozilla Common Voice is a massive, publicly available multilingual dataset of human voices designed to train speech applications. It relies on worldwide volunteer contributors who read sentences aloud and validate recordings made by others across over 100 languages, making speech technology accessible in low-resource languages.

Downloading and using dataset releases requires agreeing to the Mozilla Common Voice Terms of Use, which strictly prohibit attempting to determine the identity of speakers or re-identifying contributors.

name: Fashion-MNIST
description: Fashion-MNIST is a dataset of Zalando's article images consisting of a training set of 60,000 examples and a test set of 10,000 examples. Each example is a 28x28 grayscale image, associated with a label from 10 classes (T-shirt/top, Trouser, Pullover, Dress, Coat, Sandal, Shirt, Sneaker, Bag, Ankle boot), serving as a direct drop-in replacement for the original MNIST dataset for benchmarking machine learning algorithms.

name: ImageNet (ILSVRC 2012)
description: The ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge 2012 (ILSVRC2012) dataset is one of the most widely used benchmarks in computer vision. It contains 1,000 object categories with over 1.28 million training images, 50,000 validation images, and 100,000 test images, organized according to the WordNet hierarchy.

name: Large Movie Review Dataset (IMDb)
description: The Large Movie Review Dataset is a benchmark for binary sentiment classification containing 50,000 highly polar movie reviews from the Internet Movie Database (IMDb). It provides an even split of 25,000 reviews for training and 25,000 reviews for testing, with no more than 30 reviews per movie, alongside an additional 50,000 unlabeled reviews for unsupervised learning.

name: Iris Plants Database
description: Perhaps the best known database in pattern recognition literature, created by R.A. Fisher in 1936. Contains 150 instances (3 classes of 50 instances each) across 4 measurements: sepal length, sepal width, petal length, and petal width for three iris plant species (Iris setosa, Iris versicolour, and Iris virginica).

name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset 2.0 (SQuAD 2.0)
description: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) 2.0 combines the 100,000 questions in SQuAD 1.1 with over 50,000 unanswerable questions written adversarially by crowdworkers to look similar to answerable ones. To do well on SQuAD 2.0, systems must not only answer questions when possible, but also determine when no answer is supported by the paragraph and abstain from answering.

name: Wine Quality Dataset
description: The Wine Quality dataset includes physicochemical tests of red and white variants of the Portuguese 'Vinho Verde' wine. It contains 11 input variables describing chemical properties (such as fixed acidity, volatile acidity, citric acid, residual sugar, chlorides, and alcohol) and an output sensory score evaluated by wine experts between 0 and 10.
